Issued at 348 PM CDT Fri Sep 25 2026

Currently...

Upper air and satellite data continuing to show southwesterly
flow in place this afternoon across the area...set up between 
high pressure sitting over the TX Gulf Coast, with ridging 
extending northward through through MN, and troughing over the 
western CONUS. This troughing is being driven by a couple of 
systems, one just working its way into the Pac NW, the other 
making its way northeast out of the Desert SW/Srn Plains. During
the daytime hours so far today...any scattered showers had 
pushed east during the early morning hours, with little other 
than drizzle left behind. This has mainly affected the ENE half 
of the forecast area...where satellite has shown more stubborn 
cloud cover and area obs have shown ceilings remaining under 1k 
ft. Winds across the area remain south- southeasterly, and 
overall light, as we remain between sfc high pressure over much 
of the eastern CONUS and troughing/low pressure through the High
Plains into TX. By the time its all said and done, forecast 
highs won't work out too bad...NErn areas under more cloud cover
have struggled to get out of the mid 60s, further south has had
a few peaks of sun, and lower-mid 70s have worked their way in.

This evening through the weekend...

Seeing some showers and storms moving northward through south- 
southwestern KS, driven by increased lift associated with that
upper level shortwave disturbance roughly in the NM/CO/OK/TX 
border area. Models remain in good agreement showing this 
disturbance continuing on that northeastward track, bringing 
increasing chances for precip to the forecast area this 
evening/tonight. Aided later this evening by an increasing 
SSWrly low-level jet, forecast has pretty high chances going 
(70-90 percent)...with models continuing to focus the overall 
best chances roughly over central/eastern portions of the 
forecast area. Will be better chances for thunderstorms, with 
models showing perhaps up to 1000 j/kg nosing into the 
area...and while some storms could be on the stronger side, the 
overall threat for severe weather remains low. The main concern 
with these precip chances would be with the additional 
rainfall...if areas heavier rates happen to track over any areas
that were part of the swath of 3-5 inches from the past 2 days,
could result in some flooding concerns. 

Through the overnight hours into Saturday morning...if the
higher res models hold onto their trend, have the higher 
precipitation chances hanging on too long in the forecast. Have 
60+ percent chances lingering across areas east of HWY 281 
through sunrise Saturday...some models say activity cloud push 
east by closer to 09Z. This is talking showers/storms...not the 
potential fog/drizzle/low ceilings that could linger hours 
longer. 

Have diminishing preciptiation chances during the day on 
Saturday...but couldn't totally dry out the afternoon hours, as 
models have been pretty persistent showing another weaker push 
of mid-upper level potentially sparking off some afternoon 
showers/storms across areas mainly east of Highway 281. 
Especially for the western half of the forecast area...models 
showing better potential for more sun...the further east you go,
that will be tougher to do, especially with the chance for 
additional precip developing during the afternoon. Because of 
that uncertainty with clouds/precip, not a ton of confidence in 
the forecast highs for Saturday...which currently sit in the low
70s in the NE to low 80s in the far SSW.

Forecast finally dries out for Sunday...and models remain in
good agreement with that, as upper level ridging builds in 
across the area...set up between areas of low pressure affecting
each coast. Expecting generally partly cloudy skies, highs 
mainly in the 70s.

New work week... 

This upper level ridging centered through the Plains is short-
lived, with models in good agreement showing southwesterly 
flow returning on Monday, driven by that western CONUS upper low
that looks to dig into southern CA. Models showing that as that
low digs further south, a separate northern stream shortwave 
disturbance will be pushing through the Central/Nrn Rockies will
help drive increasing precipitation chances. Do still have a 
small area of low chances (20 percent) over far WNW portions of 
the area Monday afternoon, but the overall better chances look 
to hold off until Monday evening- overnight.

A potentially more active/wet period returns from Tuesday
on...still plenty of things to iron out in the coming days. 
Will say that compared to 24hrs ago, there is better agreement 
between models with the main upper low, its evolution and trek 
across the Central Plains. At 12Z Tuesday, this upper low looks 
to be roughly in the CA/AZ/NV border area...trekking further 
into AZ/NM by sunrise Wednesday...then turning a bit more
